name: Window cords and window falls

6-12m.rationale: CPSC's cord data cover infants and children under 5 without a split; scored lower before climbing begins.

12-24m.rationale: CPSC: about nine children under 5 die each year from window covering cords; falls data cover ages 12 and under.

24-36m.rationale: Same under-5 cord hazard; toddlers climb to windows, and falls cost lives in the 12-and-under data.

36-60m.rationale: Still under 5 for cords; no finer age split for falls.

injury_evidence.note: CPSC says about nine children under 5 die each year from strangulation in corded window coverings (its latest data at that time).
About 184 infants and young children died from window cord strangulation; CPSC knew of more than 100 non-fatal incidents.
About 5,600 children 12 and under were treated in emergency departments for window falls in 2024, about one in three needing hospitalization; at least 25 died from window falls in 2021-2023.

why_it_matters: Dangling blind cords can strangle young children, and open windows within reach can lead to serious falls. Moving furniture, shortening cords and limiting how far windows open reduces the risk.

fix_steps.text: Move cribs, beds, chairs and other climbable furniture away from windows.
Keep cords well out of reach and as short as possible, and open windows from the top rather than the bottom when you can.
Anchor continuous-loop cords tight to the wall or floor with a tension device, and adjust cord stops on inner cords.
Request a free retrofit repair kit from the Window Covering Safety Council (800-506-4636 or windowcoverings.org); some kits do not fix a dangling pull cord.
Install window stops so windows open no more than four inches. Do not rely on screens to keep a child in.
Install window guards that adults can open in a fire; renters should ask the landlord.
Replace corded window coverings with cordless ones in rooms where young children sleep or play.

reminder.text: Check window cords, stops and guards, and that furniture has not been moved under a window.

verify_rule: Window coverings have no reachable cords, windows open no more than four inches or have guards, and no climbable furniture stands under them.
blind_spots: Cord length and inner cords behind shades
Whether window stops or guards actually hold
Windows in other rooms and at relatives' homes
